root_cause.text: Improper error handling in `mana_ib_create_qp_rss()` where the loop counter `i` was incorrectly decremented twice on the `mana_create_wq_obj()` failure path, and the WQ object created by `mana_create_wq_obj()` was not destroyed when `mana_ib_install_cq_cb()` failed, leading to resource leaks and potential use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the extra `i--` inside the `if (ret)` block after `mana_create_wq_obj()` (which caused a double decrement when combined with the cleanup loop) and adds an explicit `mana_destroy_wq_obj()` call before `goto fail` in the `mana_ib_install_cq_cb()` failure path to ensure the WQ object is cleaned up.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one cleanup error by removing erroneous decrement of loop index when a WQ object creation fails.
intent_record.what: Removed the decrement of loop index i and associated comment in the error handling path of mana_create_wq_obj call.
intent_record.how: Previously, on failure, the index was decremented before jumping to the fail label, potentially causing the cleanup loop to skip the last successfully created object. Now the index is not decremented, so cleanup can correctly cover all successful objects up to the failed index.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by destroying the work queue object before jumping to fail when mana_ib_install_cq_cb fails in mana_ib_create_qp_rss.
intent_record.what: Added call to mana_destroy_wq_obj before goto fail when mana_ib_install_cq_cb fails in mana_ib_create_qp_rss.
intent_record.how: Prevents resource leak by freeing the work queue object (wq->rx_object) on the error path before going to the fail label.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `mana_ib_create_qp_rss`, the error handling after `mana_create_wq_obj` failure uses `i--; goto fail;` (line ~208) combined with `while (i-- > 0)` cleanup in `fail` (line ~280). This double decrements the loop counter, causing off-by-one cleanup that may skip destroying the last successfully created WQ object. Additionally, if the later `kzalloc` for `gdma_cq` fails (line ~241), the WQ object for that index is not destroyed because `i` is not adjusted and the cleanup loop fails to include it. The fix (proper single decrement and explicit cleanup of the current WQ on failure) is not present in this commit.
